# PR11: isolated login, no real credentials issued

17-sep-2026 ART. Request:Implement isolated login without issuing real credentials.

[PR11](https://github.com/gatehot59-star/corpus-legal-tarija/pull/11) stacks on PR10. Base2fd265827b984c85f36fa7d539ef006a6fe05b47. Tested published code18111862c729b4bfcb32b1087dcb279d01c47dd2. No merge, deployment, live Corpus/VM/service changes, real accounts or real credential issuance. The only session tokens created were ephemeral fixture tokens inside temporary test databases; those databases and listeners are cleaned up. No tokens are included in this receipt or delivered to the user.

## Architecture and decisions

New sistema/api/isolated_login.py wraps PR10's make_app; tests/test_isolated_login.py exercises it over real loopback HTTP. .github/workflows/clean-snapshot.yml adds these paths, compilation and a90s test timeout, retaining earlier suites, checkout SHA,contents:read and persist-credentials:false. No changes to access_policy.py,exact_http.py,version_text.py or servidor.py. No new package dependency, automatic migration, listener, production container or UI.

IsolatedLoginApp(candidate,store,collection,enable_test_login=False,clock=time.time) is disabled by default. It requires explicit opt-in, a loopback REMOTE_ADDR, an existing separate store marked isolated_test, and fixture-* account IDs. These are administrative guardrails, not containment against a malicious operator. A local proxy or tunnel could make external traffic look local:DO NOT mount this behind any public proxy/tunnel. The host WSGI environment and store are trusted.

LOGIN_SCHEMA declares login_environment,login_passwords and a singleton login_budget on the PR10 store. Schema is applied only by test fixtures, not at import/startup. No signup/provisioning endpoint exists. The password verifier is scrypt N=2^17,r=8,p=1,dklen32,16byte salt,OpenSSL maxmem256MiB. [OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) was checked live this turn and lists this configuration when Argon2id is unavailable. scrypt preserves the repository's stdlib-only runtime. This is not a new CVE audit of Python/OpenSSL/host.

Unknown and disabled users perform a full KDF and receive the same401body as a wrong password. hmac.compare_digest compares the verifier; this does NOT prove whole-request constant timing or eliminate all enumeration side channels. Test salts/passwords are explicitly fictional; no real password was hashed/provisioned.

## HTTP contract and trust flow

POST /api/v2/login,Content-Type:application/json,body exactly username/password. Username lowercase ASCII letters/digits/_/- up to80;password1..1024UTF8bytes. Body requires Content-Length1..4096. Reject duplicate keys,nonobjects,extra keys,invalid types,Origin and Transfer-Encoding. No cookies,CORS or browser login UI. JSON responses have no-store and nosniff. Errors never include traceback,password or token.

Request -> explicit isolation/loopback check -> bounded JSON -> store marker -> persisted attempt budget -> account verifier -> session INSERT -> commit -> return fixture bearer token. Subsequent reads go through the existing PR10 policy. Login writes NO AccessGrant,so a logged-in user without a grant still gets403. All test grants are explicit fictitious insertions performed by the fixture,not login.

Session token:secrets.token_urlsafe(32),256bits random input,900sTTL,only SHA256stored in access_sessions. A subsequent login gets a fresh token regardless of any supplied Authorization header. The bearer is returned once to the in-process test client and is never logged or commiteado. The temporary token is meaningful only for the temporary fixture store,not live Corpus.

A BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction serializes attempt-budget/KDF/session writes in one store. All accounts share a coarse limit of5attempts per60s,including successful attempts;sixth attempt gets429before KDF. Attempts persist across requests,window resets at60s and clock rollback/nonfinite time fails closed. This deliberately restrictive test budget is not a production per-account/IP/distributed abuse-control system. It can deny service to another fixture user. KDF work under the write transaction also limits throughput;10x load/concurrency not measured.

Responses:200fixture session,400malformed body,401generic credentials,403isolation/origin/framing rejection,405method,415content type,429budget,503internal/store/clock failure. Read failures retain PR9/PR10 behavior.

## Limits and remaining work

This is isolated engineering progress in the accounts/session integration,not D09/M03/pilot completion. No real user/credential provisioning,password reset,MFA,logout HTTP,account UI,grant issuance,acta verification or payments. Existing PR10session revocation was tested via direct fixture updates,not a logout endpoint. No TLS,production audit logging or deployment configuration.

WSGI body read is bounded in size but relies on the hosting server for socket/slow-body timeout;no slowloris/hostile concurrency certification. Do not expose wsgiref or this module publicly. No filesystem protection against malicious same-user replacement or trustworthy-operator bypass. No hardening claim for historic secrets or OS/CVEs. No timing/SLA,distributed revocation or response recall claim. Reset/logout and authorized provisioning remain future work;real issuance still needs a separate explicit decision.
